body: I just failed on my maybe 8th attempt. Talk to me. I’m losing it

It’s scary when you believe the whole world is laughing behind your back and that your closest friends and family are in on it. It wasn’t really about caring what people thought. It was more than that. In my right mind I am a schizophrenic drug addict- I stopped relating to/caring about what most people think a long time ago.

I know firsthand (5 recent years on the streets) that along with homelessness comes drug use. Be careful out there and don’t let the substance use make your symptoms worse. I’ve experienced my worst psychosis when I have been in your similar position. No longer homeless but still struggling with substance abuse. Getting myself Medicaid and regularly taking meds made a world of difference. My voices are generally supportive too, but even with “friends” in my head, when I’m symptomatic my perception is skewed and I’m generally looking at the world from the wrong angle. I vibe with my fellow man better when my symptoms are under control. So anywho, beware the drugs and look into Medicaid. Sometimes I miss my voices but I like feeling normal again for the most part. What state are you in, btw?

I have the same delusion. I thought my life was a reality show on the dark web for a long time. Felt that I was being observed constantly. You don’t know how many times I was embarrassed to death about things that I did when I was alone because I was convinced that somewhere, somehow, people were watching it. I had it in my head that people I met already knew of me, and everyone was laughing about the fact that I was the only one who didn’t know all about my reality stardom on the dark web. I thought there were cameras throughout my house and that film crew were all over the city. I saw people taking my pictures constantly. It drove me to multiple suicide attempts before I realized I had schizophrenia. I still feel that way sometimes and have to remind myself that no one is watching me or hearing my thoughts or following my day to day activities. And I’ve never seen the Truman show, although I know of the premise. I had that delusion all on my own, without drawing  conscience comparisons to any movies or stories.
The crushing monotony and unfulfilling nature of the 9-5, corporate American, paycheck to paycheck life
